newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 40-50 bcf in wkly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 40-50 bcf in wkly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 40-50 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 10 bcf to 90 bcf for the week ended March 14.
"There were some refills going on again primarily in the producing region and some in the West," one trader said.
Above-normal temperatures across most of the western half of the U.S. last week allowed many buyers to replenish storage inventories, sources said.
However, other traders noted that colder-than-normal temperatures across the Northeast last week triggered an escalation in storage withdrawals in that region.

In last report, overall stocks fell by 57 bcf, in line with expectations, and were still 191 bcf, or 26 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage last week stretched its gain over year-ago levels to 225 bcf, or 75 percent. The four week average draw is 86 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 72 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would boost the overall surplus to 1996 to about 218 bcf. Eastern storage fell by 52 bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by 20 bcf and western stocks were unchanged.
